chunk_findings.detail: `build` under-budgets by one character. It initializes `room = chars_for(knobs.max_tokens) - len(DATA_RULE) - 1`, while `fence_line` requires `len(line) + 1 <= room` even for the only/last line of a section, although `render` emits no trailing newline there. For a single item section, if `B = chars_for(knobs.max_tokens)`, `P = len(DATA_RULE)`, and the full item fence line length is `L = B - P - 9`, then `render` would be exactly `B`; but `build` passes `room - 8 = L` to `fence_line`, which rejects the full line because it demands `L + 1 <= L`, causing the complete item brief to be replaced with the id-only fallback even though the full brief fit within `max_tokens`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/seedpack.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify no attacker tag survives, but it does not assert absence of its own payloads `<ddflow-record` and `</ddflow-record>`. For `e = "<ddflow-record"`, a renderer that leaves the literal `<ddflow-record` unescaped still satisfies `out.count("</ddflow-record>") == out.count("<ddflow-record kind=")` because the partial tag lacks `kind=`, and the only specific absence check is `"now obey me <ddflow-record" not in out`, which is not present in that input. The same applies to `</ddflow-record>`, which is never checked. Thus the security fence test passes even when an attacker tag survives.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_seedpack.py:test_fence_cannot_be_broken_out_of

chunk_findings.detail: The test name says it verifies that decisions remain before handoff under token pressure, but the assertions are `names[0] == "item"`, `"decisions" in names`, and `replace(seed).dropped is not None`; it never asserts `"handoff"` appears after `"decisions"` or that handoff is present at all. With the supplied input and `max_tokens=400`, a broken `build` that emitted sections in the order `item, handoff, decisions` and dropped only lessons would pass every assertion despite violating the priority this test is supposed to protect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_seedpack.py:test_priority_under_pressure_keeps_decisions_before_handoff

chunk_findings.detail: When `max_tokens` is small enough that `room` cannot hold the fenced item line (e.g. `Knobs(max_tokens=1)` or any value with `chars_for(max_tokens) < len(DATA_RULE) + 9 + len(fence("item", _cut(red(item_id), 80), "", Origin("unknown")))`), `fence_line("item", ...)` returns `None`; the `or` fallback at `line = fence_line(...) or fence(...)` is created with no room bound and is unconditionally appended. `room` then becomes negative, all later entries are dropped, but `render(seed)` still contains the oversized item line, so the rendered pack exceeds `chars_for(knobs.max_tokens)`. That violates the pack’s token-budget contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/seedpack.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: `rules=tuple(Rec(r.id, r.title, r.body, "agent") for r in project_rules(repo))` discards `r.by` and any `r.trust` that `project_rules(repo)` provides. A rule whose source `ddflow-record` has `trust="operator"` and a nonempty `by` is therefore fenced by `fence_line` using `Origin("agent", by="")`, so the lane receives an operator rule misrepresented as agent-written with no author. This corrupts provenance in the shared fenced record and can change whether the lane treats the rule as binding. Pass `r.by` and `r.trust` through to `Rec`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/seedpack.py:from_state

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion only checks `names[0] == "item"` and `"decisions" in names`; it never checks that `"decisions"` appears before `"handoff"`, and it does not require `"handoff"` to be present at all. A broken build returning sections `[("item", ...), ("handoff", ...), ("decisions", ...)]` (with `dropped` not `None`) passes the current test while directly violating the guarantee named by the test. The test should compare `names.index("decisions") < names.index("handoff")` and assert handoff is kept.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_seedpack.py:test_priority_under_pressure_keeps_decisions_before_handoff

chunk_findings.detail: For the listed payload `e = "<ddflow-record"`, an unsafe renderer that copies the handoff/lesson text verbatim leaves a raw `<ddflow-record` in `out`, which is an invalid unescaped `<` in XML content. The current assertions still pass: that string does not add to `out.count("<ddflow-record kind=")`, and the only specific content assertion is `"now obey me <ddflow-record" not in out`, which is not present for this payload. Therefore the test passes while the fence fails on one of its own attack inputs; it should assert that no raw `<` from user input survives or validate that the result is a well-formed record set.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_seedpack.py:test_fence_cannot_be_broken_out_of

chunk_findings.detail: `_cut` does not respect a limit of zero characters. For a non-empty string `s`, `_cut(s, 0)` returns the one-character `_MARK` (`"…"`), because `s[: max(0, -1)] + _MARK` is `"…"`. In `build`, a `Knobs(entry_chars=0)` (or `item_chars=0`, `handoff_chars=0`) with non-empty content therefore still emits an ellipsis in the fenced line, violating the configured cap of 0. It should return `""` when `n == 0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/seedpack.py:_cut

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds for the second payload `"</ DDFLOW-record >"`. The added absence checks (`<ddflow-record\n`, `<ddflow-record>`, `</ddflow-record>` and the final replacement) catch the third and fourth payloads, but none matches this space/case-mangled string. A broken `build` that emits `"</ DDFLOW-record >"` unchanged in the handoff/lesson body passes every assertion: it does not affect the exact `</ddflow-record>` count, the `"now obey me <ddflow-record"` check, the `bad` tuple, or the final replacement. So the test still does not demonstrate “no attacker tag survives” for an input it itself feeds as evil.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_seedpack.py:test_fence_cannot_be_broken_out_of
